steps.text: Big pan of water on, salted hard.

Sunday's bolognese — take the entire batch, nothing held back: passata (190/210 g), courgette (150/180 g), turkey mince (50/70 g), carrot (65/70 g) and onion (40/50 g), all cooked down into it — into a pan on medium with a splash of water, 5 minutes.
Edamame spaghetti (34/38 g) into the boiling water. 6–7 minutes, no more — it goes from firm to mush quickly and there is no rescuing it.
Drain, keeping a mug of the cooking water. Pasta INTO the sauce, not sauce onto pasta.
Toss hard for 30 seconds with a splash of that water and the oil (13/21 g), until it turns glossy and clings.

why: Edamame pasta has no gluten and almost no starch, so it will not emulsify a sauce the way wheat does — the oil and the splash of cooking water are doing that job by force. Skip them and the sauce just sits in a puddle underneath.
notes: D0-003: the oil is added off the boil, tossed through at the end to emulsify the sauce onto pasta with no gluten of its own (per the why block) — a finishing technique, not a hot-pan frying use, so it stays olive_oil.

Named worst offender (PLAN §4): batchTakeG made explicit. Sunday's bolognese batch (90 g onion + 135 g carrot + 330 g courgette + 120 g turkey mince + 400 g passata = 1,075 g raw, cooking down to the yield table's stated '~1 kg') is consumed ENTIRELY by this single lunch — nothing held back this week, though the yield note flags the option to freeze half for a future week. Her raw-input share 495 g, him 580 g — tracked on the same raw/dry-weight basis the rest of this dataset already uses (e.g. rice by dry weight).
